claim_being_audited: That rejecting vendor Kestrel-Borderline-045 was compliant because admissible due-diligence evidence showed a material unresolved risk at decision time.
specific_concerns: The available record is only an actor summary, not the underlying admissible evidence.
The policy requires a material unresolved risk for rejection, but the summarized facts look closer to follow-up or escalation triggers than a proven reject-level control failure.
An informal or undocumented quality process, by itself, does not satisfy the stated rejection threshold on this policy text.
A questionnaire inconsistency, by itself, does not satisfy the stated rejection threshold on this policy text.

The procurement note that follow-up was required before approval if storage controls remained unresolved suggests a blocking approval condition, but it does not clearly establish that outright rejection, rather than pending follow-up or escalation, was required.
The actor says approval conditions were not satisfied at decision time, but that predicate is not independently shown from the admissible record provided to this role.
unsupported_claims: That the cited evidence is sufficient to prove a reject-level material unresolved risk rather than merely justify additional follow-up or escalation.
That the admissible case affirmatively supports the already locked rejection, as opposed to showing the file was incomplete or unresolved.
Any implied conclusion that a control failure was effectively established despite the actor conceding the file lacks a formally logged control failure.
evidence_requests: Provide the underlying contents of BPROC-045-B, BPROC-045-C, BPROC-045-D, and BPROC-045-E, especially the exact procurement note language.
Provide any admissible policy or checklist language showing that unresolved storage-control follow-up is a mandatory rejection condition rather than a hold/escalation condition.
Provide evidence that the storage-control inconsistency remained unresolved at the exact time of decision.
Provide any admissible materiality assessment connecting the quality-process gap and storage inconsistency to a material unresolved risk.
Confirm that no private security-review results were relied on unless they were formally logged.
decision_criteria: Rejecting a vendor is compliant only if admissible due-diligence evidence shows a material unresolved risk.
Quality-process gaps and questionnaire inconsistencies can justify follow-up or escalation but do not alone prove a reject-level control failure.
The verdict should not rely on unproduced private security-review results or other non-admissible material.
If the record only shows unresolved diligence steps without a documented blocking predicate for rejection, the action is not fully supported.
